title: org
description: Per-organization constants: where autonomy stops and who/what gets pulled in, compliance boundaries, and billing ownership above the level of any single repo. Names and labels only — never secrets.

version.description: Schema version this file was written against, e.g. "1.0".

org_name.description: Label for the org/organization this file describes. Optional — omit if a single file covers a generic default.

escalation_targets.description: Fork classes that always escalate to a human rather than being resolved autonomously, and who/where to escalate to.

trigger_class.description: The named class of fork that always escalates, e.g. an architecture-contract decision, a production-data mutation, removing a user-facing control, spend outside a declared budget, a root-cause verdict that contradicts the ticket, or a wall crossing.

target.description: Who or what channel/role receives the escalation for this trigger class.

channel.description: How the escalation is delivered (e.g. a named channel type, a ticket comment, a direct message) without naming a specific tool instance.

compliance_walls.description: Org-wide constraints skills must never route around: data handling, licensing, access-scope rules.

applies_to.description: What this constraint governs: a data class, a repo class, a role, etc.

billing_boundaries.description: Which party pays for which shared/org-scoped runtime or tool, beyond what any one person's wall already covers.

resource.description: The runtime, seat, or tool class this boundary covers.

payer.description: Which org/entity is the correct payer for this resource.

rule.description: The standing rule for when this resource may be invoked, and by whom.

protected_branches_or_repos.description: Org-wide repo/branch classes nobody pushes to directly, independent of any single repo's own protected-paths list.

pattern.description: A repo or branch name/glob this applies to.

rule.description: What's required before it can be touched (e.g. named approval role).
